The Rider Panel: 500 AI cyclists shopping for a smart trainer

The Rider Panel tests how buyers respond to a new product before it launches. For this first study we recruited 500 UK cyclists who will shop for an indoor trainer between September and March, from a potentially limitless pool of shoppers the Rider Panel can draw on. Each one is an AI agent with a written life story and a budget to stick to. They live the season month by month in their own town's real weather. They choose from the trainers someone like them would actually come across, at real UK prices.

What the study found

The results of four launch plans for a new smart trainer

We invented a brand called Northfold and a folding smart trainer, the DD1. Northfold isn't a real company. The DD1 turns your own bike into an indoor exercise bike. It's quiet and accurate. It folds flat to 14cm deep for small homes. Like its main rivals, it comes with the Zwift Cog and Click. It goes on sale on 16 November at £499. Sigma Sports and Tredz stock it, with a display stand in Halfords.

We ran the same season four times on the same 500 shoppers. Their lives stayed the same between runs. So did the weather and every rival's price. Only the Northfold launch changed, so any difference in what they bought comes from that one decision.

Ranges come from re-sampling the 500 shoppers 4,000 times. A change counts when its range stays clear of zero. Revenue is Northfold's revenue from the 500 shoppers.

    Who the 500 are

    Who the 500 shoppers are

    The panel isn't every cyclist. Most cyclists never think about an indoor trainer in a given year. These 500 are the ones who go shopping for one this season. We built 200,000 UK cyclists from survey data first. Then we gave each of them a chance of shopping this season based on what they ride indoors now and what's wrong with it. The 500 were drawn from everyone who shops, so their mix follows from the real population. About 2 in every 100 adult cyclists shop for a trainer in a season. Four in ten of these shoppers are buying their first. Five hundred was our choice for a first study. The pool has no limit, so a brand's study can be as large as its question needs.

    Each shopper is an AI agent, not a persona on a slide. Their life story covers work and family. Their profile records the bike computer they own and how much its brand matters to them. It also records the cassette on their bike and where a trainer would live at home. Their kit never appears in their life story, so it can't take over the plot. This first panel is set in the UK. For another country, every input comes from that country instead.

    How a study works

    How a Rider Panel study works, in four steps

    1. Draw 500 shoppers from survey data

      Draw the people who shop for your category this season from a simulated population built on survey data.

    2. Load the real market

      Load each town's real weather with the retail calendar. Add every rival at its real price.

    3. Write each launch plan

      Your product and price. Your shops and reviews. Write each version of the launch you want to compare.

    4. Run the season once per plan

      Every shopper lives the season month by month and keeps a diary. The difference between runs is what your decision changes.

    Accuracy checks

    How we checked the results

    We set the pass marks before any results came in, so we couldn't move them afterwards. Here is every check, including the two the panel narrowly missed.

    Sales in real units

    What the results mean in real sales

    Each shopper stands for about real UK shoppers. That's set so the £499 run's trainer sales match the size of the UK market this season. Our market figure is an estimate, so put in your own if you have one.

    Our estimate is about 185,000 indoor trainers a year, worked out from market revenue, with low confidence. September to March carries 65% of a year's UK trainer searches, which gives about 120,000.

    Northfold's first-season reach is capped at the awareness of JetBlack, an established UK challenger brand. A new brand can't be better known than that in its first season.

    Northfold DD1 sales, September to March

    Ranges come from the panel only. They don't include doubt about the market's size.

    Why it matters

    How the Rider Panel compares with focus groups and surveys

    Asking real customers is slow and expensive, so most brands only do it for their biggest launches. Everything else gets decided on instinct. The Rider Panel makes testing a launch cheap enough to do every time, before you spend money on stock and campaigns.

    Focus groups and surveysThe Rider Panel
    Time to an answerWeeks to recruit and runA few days
    Testing what-ifsOne version per study. Each change means a new study.Change the price or a channel, then rerun the same season on the same people
    CompetitorsHard to show a realistic market in a roomEvery rival at its real price, including its Black Friday deal
    TimingPeople guess what they'd do in three monthsShoppers live the season month by month, in real weather
    Why people decideWhat people say in front of othersEach shopper's own reasons, plus what would change their mind
    Real customersYesNo. It tells you which plans are worth taking to them.
